newsitem.title: EGYPT: Suez Steel investors will get 23 pct of shares.
newsitem.headline: Suez Steel investors will get 23 pct of shares.

text.p: A public offering of 30 percent of the equity in new Egyptian firm Suez Steel was oversubscribed more than three times, the agents of the sale said on Wednesday.

The agents, National Bank of Egypt, said investors would be allocated 23 percent of the shares they applied for, with fractions rounded up in favour of the smallest investors. The 360,000 shares have a fixed price of 100 pounds ($29.46) each.
The rest of the 1.2 million shares are owned by the founders of the steel company -- two state-owned banks, six companies and one individual.
Investors need pay only a quarter of the nominal value now and the firm will ask for the rest within five years from the date of establishment.
The firm, to be set up in the Red Sea province of Suez, will produce steel billets, they added. It has forecast a return on capital of not less than 20 percent a year.
